classification.difficultyReason: Invent an unprompted tilting construction that measures one-sixth of a tank using adjacent vertices, recognise the resulting corner tetrahedron, and transfer its 20 litres to leave exactly 100 litres.

content.prompt: I have two identical tanks in the shape of right rectangular prisms, each capable of holding 120 litres. I need to fill one of these tanks with exactly 100 litres of water. Explain how I can do this if I simply have a hose to fill the tanks and no measuring devices. There are no markings on the tanks to indicate how full they are.

answer.short: Fill one tank. Tilt the empty tank with a corner lowest, and transfer water into it until the surface passes through the three vertices adjacent to that corner. This transfers $\frac16\times120=20$ litres, leaving 100 litres in the first tank.
answer.worked:
Fill tank A completely. Hold empty tank B with one bottom corner lowest. Tilt it so the three vertices joined by edges to that corner lie in a horizontal plane. Pour water from A into B until the surface reaches those three vertices.

The water in B forms a triangular-based pyramid. If the tank dimensions are $l$, $w$ and $h$, its triangular base has area $\frac12lw$ and its perpendicular height is $h$.
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{water in B}}&=\frac13\left(\frac12lw\right)h\\V_{\text{water in B}}&=\frac16lwh\\V_{\text{water in B}}&=\frac16(120)\\V_{\text{water in B}}&=20\text{ L}.\end{align*}$$
Tank A therefore contains $120-20=100$ litres.
